## Design

### 2026-10-09 – I learned a lot from this session!

**2.5h**

I learned a lot from this session!

I started off by downloading KiCad, setting it up and adding my libraries.

In the 30ish mins it took to download, I researched what PCBs actually are and are made of (lasagna of fiberglass and copper with holes). I also looked into a refresher on basic electrical stuff. I understand WAY better now what voltage vs amps vs power is. Basically voltage gives the electrical potential, amps is the rate charge flows at, and power is the rate at which energy is transferred. And different components on my PCB will draw different amount of amps at the same voltage to change how much energy flows through them!

then I spent an embarrassing amount of time trying to understand what net labels are. After slightly more than an hour, I had... the schematic for a single microcontroller done.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 203222](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/1ea9feb70ebead86625514a870f6389dfcdf02a935404eb5218bcc4e92bf02f4.png)
(you can likely see my frustration from the label for this...)

But after that things went a lot more smoothly! It took about 30-45 mins to get the other 3 components done, and I learned how signal wires use electricity to transmit data (two different voltages represent 0 and 1)! And I learned that the SCL wire on the 4 and 8 pin thingies is like a CPU clock and synchronizes data transfer and the SDA is a serial data transmitter that transmits data one bit at a time!

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 203946](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/7ba6192f87f99d84f3438480210bdd41f8eac0c70cb38d0cdb339df3815aa56e.png)
extensive googling...

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 205942](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/70e72b8d25fe0e05e909d96e24575a996862bf1889bb79ba9bedd491e8d13fb0.png)
My finished schematic!

After painfully typing out every single footprint name, I finally had my components in the PCB editor.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 210729](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/230428c920c08e508f696dfc642a15f031eabe5060f6b4e7ed5e1192bf4e8891.png)

I then spent way too long tracing out every single line on my star until I liked the way it looked.

![Screenshot 2026-10-09 212403](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/f09b0c3ea005e34606e14222cae06a926d8db3b4d402bf84e602997fc16f970e.png)

This was my stopping point for the day! This project is frustrating but super fun. I wish I knew better how everything worked but I'm sure it'll come with time. I'm excited to get back to work tomorrow but it's like nighttime and i'm tired so i'm going to sleep and dream of PCBs now.

### 2026-10-10 – Today was wiring hell(TM).

**2.5h**

Today was wiring hell(TM).

I started by arranging all of my components on the board in a way that seemed space efficient (more on this later). Then i realized my board was too big and I tried to resize it then I realized it wasn't lined up with the grid so i started trying to individually line up every single line segment. I eventually gave up and called it a day.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 175145](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/cb620704cf69cbb761550322a1ea10ea2dec336ab7d8f065fd9bb52a75125975.png)
I then began the wiring process and OH BOY did I not know what I was doing. My first way of organizing did NOT account for the fact that there would be, you know, WIRES CONNECTING THE COMPONENTS.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 183600](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/17b98d744bcc37dce43fe4baaf93e79d8e912b8769ed1b85b05b287642b7e087.png)
my horrendous first attempt.

After this attempt, I realized that the blue lines were meant to HELP YOU and I actually tried to rearrange the components so that stuff that was wired together was close together. I also realized the board had 2 sides that I could utilize when wires crossed! This fixed everything, right?

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 184932](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/515b642151a0ea5540948eb6121ecbf47f09ac7c23dc5e08437a29f06c74516f.png)
Closer, but still not there.

At this point, I realized the big roadblock was the microcontroller. SO MANY THINGS connected to it and it only could be wired on one side. On my next attempt, I tried to do as much on the back side as possible to account for this.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 191753](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/c85089b284cb027c572ce2588764c88616516d6caed698cf6a50967497f0f731.png)
ONE WIRE. I was ONE WIRE AWAY.

I rearranged my components for the final time and locked in. Finally...

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 192458](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/c01c5cc31746ecbdf73ea5c7d6b30c569a80c7f9d55d7ed6114cc2919071a16d.png)
The layout was complete! Or so I thought.

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 194044](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/e2ff30f0ac8f3f15bbff01c174dad37bf80ca1076a901eb6ceda06979e799ef8.png)
After running the DRC, I realized that the pretty text and outlines around my components were not cosmetic. They were the SILKSCREEN and supposed to go ON THE PCB.

I spent some time trying to fix some errors, but I still have to adjust my layout a bit. Which will likely redoing the wiring one more time at least.

At least  I got some good work in today.

### 2026-10-11 – Today I finished the project!

**3h**

Today I finished the project!

I started off by adjusting the positions of the components to fix the errors  I got yesterday. After a quick rewire, my PCB was done.

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 123601](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/3e4b4583172940ddacc0b5f489499345523070df81fbefe0fcab24c26e3e9861.png)

There was still a lot of warnings about the silkscreen being clipped; I spent about 20 minutes trying to figure out how to fix them but eventually gave up when I realized warnings don't matter.

After that, I figured out how to use Image Converter, then I imported some images and added them to my silkscreen. I added a bunch of stars and a silly little guy.

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 135255](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/e72450247cfd4389f29bd670f2342e84618bf87a8af2abacd2eaac117d2a8f76.png)

Then I downloaded Arduino and did the firmware. I didn't change much from the tutorial, but i DID make my own silly little sprite!

![pixil-frame-01](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/5fa6572c0fd4ddd71f09cc8fe7cf3777a37641e2a3c40f6f6539c614fa6d732b.png)
I cycled through a few designs before landing on a sun. Because my Starbie's name is Sunny because the sun is a star and yeah.

Finally, I did my bill of materials. It took a WHILE to get under the $30 limit b/c of shipping costs, but I got it done!

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 194940](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/sE7vZfeaqmfwXllHYiqPgB7QRPGwMqyP/43d30c6f0a2293ec5fc69649540029bc44448b3e47415b06a809006b8afa20e1.png)

i'm so hyped to build this thing and even more hyped for CAD week! I actually have a lot of experience w/ CAD. I'm hoping to 3D print a case for my Starbie!!
